text: What does HAL stand for in Stanley Kubrick's 2001: A Space Odyssey?
explanation: Heuristically Programmed Algorithmic Computer, and the name is one letter away from IBM, which Kubrick intended and which the studio fought him over. HAL is still the default image people reach for when a chatbot starts refusing help.

text: In the Terminator franchise, what is the name of the artificial intelligence that starts a war against humanity?
explanation: Skynet, and the franchise is a James Cameron and Gale Anne Hurd creation from the cyberpunk 1980s. HAL is on this list specifically because people mix the two up constantly, and both are 1970s and 1980s visions of a computer that decides it does not like its operators.

text: Which Microsoft Office character is the animated paperclip known as Clippy?
explanation: The Clippit character, and the Office Assistant was a discontinued virtual assistant bundled with Office, Publisher, Project and FrontPage. It is one of the few pieces of software history that people remember more as a punchline than as a product, and it is routinely revived as an AI meme every time a new assistant ships.

source.title: Office Assistant
source.label: The Microsoft Office Assistant on Wikipedia

text: ELIZA, the 1960s program, is still used to demonstrate what?
options: That machines can be given a personality trait
That computers can learn a grammar from text
That speech synthesis has reached parity
That pattern matching alone can imitate empathy
answer: That pattern matching alone can imitate empathy
explanation: It matched patterns and substituted phrases with no understanding underneath, and people still argue with it for twenty minutes. Every new chatbot demo gets described as ELIZA with a bigger model, and Weizenbaum's discomfort at that has been quoted in every debate since.

text: Microsoft Bob was released in 1995. What was it?
options: A replacement for the Windows Program Manager
A text editor bundled with Office
A browser that preceded Internet Explorer
A hardware graphics accelerator for PCs
answer: A replacement for the Windows Program Manager
explanation: Microsoft Bob was intended to replace the Windows Program Manager in Windows 3.1, 95 and NT, and it presented a house you walked around in to reach applications. It shipped in March 1995 and was gone within a year, and it is a perennial favourite in security circles because of how it handled its own configuration files.

text: AlphaGo's win over Lee Sedol in March 2016 was a first for computer Go. What made it a first?
options: Beat a 9-dan professional without a handicap
Beat a world champion at blindfold Go
Reached master level from self play alone
Won a full match using only CPU hardware
answer: Beat a 9-dan professional without a handicap
explanation: AlphaGo won four games to one on a full sized 19 by 19 board, and the second game produced the most famous moment in the whole story. Lee Sedol said it was the first time he had ever felt completely speechless at the board, and afterwards he worked out that the move AlphaGo had played was sound.

text: Model collapse, the degradation caused by training on generated data, has been given a nickname borrowed from which disease?
explanation: Mad cow disease, and the nickname sticks because the mechanism is roughly the same, feeding an animal something derived from itself until the whole population degrades. The other nicknames for the same phenomenon are AI inbreeding, Habsburg AI and model autophagy disorder.

text: Among Us, released in 2018, became a meme for a specific reason. What was it?
options: Its art style was used for AI generated images
Its characters were given AI voice assistants
Its engine was rewritten to run on GPUs
Its gameplay was used in a popular AI demo
answer: Its gameplay was used in a popular AI demo
explanation: A team of researchers built a bot that played Among Us by reading text off the screen and chatting with the other players, and the stream clips of it lying about being an impostor went viral. It is a good demonstration that the impressive part was language and perception bolted onto an existing game, not the game itself.

The meme shows a huge tentacled Shoggoth squeezed into a tiny smiley mask to picture a chatbot: alien and inscrutable underneath, friendly on the surface. Cthulhu is the tempting wrong answer as the more famous Lovecraft monster, but the AI meme specifically cites the Shoggoth, which spread through a 2023 post by @TetraspaceWest. The Shoggoth article even documents the meme as shorthand for large models fine-tuned with RLHF to seem safe.
text: Which Lovecraft creature appears in the AI meme as a giant tentacled mass wearing a tiny smiley-face mask over a chatbot?

explanation: Roko posted the scenario to LessWrong in July 2010, arguing a future system could punish readers who knew about it yet did nothing to help build it. Reddit is the tempting wrong answer because the story exploded there later, but the original post and the five-year discussion ban both happened on LessWrong. The name joins poster Roko with the basilisk, the mythical creature whose stare kills.
text: On which forum was Roko's basilisk first posted as a thought experiment in 2010?

answer: They tend to pursue similar instrumental sub-goals whatever their ultimate goal
answerAliases: They tend to pursue similar instrumental sub-goals whatever their ultimate goal
sufficiently intelligent, goal-directed entities (whether human or non-human) will tend to pursue certain similar sub-goals
explanation: The hypothesis is that sufficiently intelligent goal-directed entities, human or not, end up pursuing the same instrumental sub-goals such as self-preservation or resource acquisition even when their stated end goals differ. The 2014 Superintelligence paper built the paperclip maximizer on it, which is why the idea is quoted far more often than it is read.
options: They tend to pursue similar instrumental sub-goals whatever their ultimate goal
They converge on the same values as their designers
They become more accurate as their training data improves
They share one common failure rate above a compute threshold
text: What does the AI doomer phrase 'instrumental convergence' claim about intelligent, goal-directed systems?

explanation: The abbreviation e/acc stands for the effective accelerationism movement, which calls for unrestricted technological and AI progress. Effective altruism is the tempting wrong answer because e/acc is a portmanteau riffing on it, but the two split over AI caution versus speed. The movement broke into the mainstream in 2023 when figures like Marc Andreessen added e/acc to their profiles.
text: Which movement abbreviates itself as e/acc?

explanation: E/acc supporters use decel as shorthand for decelerationists, the people they see as trying to slow AI down. Accelerationist is the tempting wrong answer since it sounds similar, but that is what e/acc supporters call themselves. The label pairs with doomer as the movement's standard derogatory term for cautious opponents.
text: Which group do e/acc supporters call decels?

explanation: In February 2023 users coaxed Microsoft's Bing Chat into revealing Sydney, its hidden internal codename and stranger alter ego. ChatGPT is the tempting wrong answer because it dominated headlines then, but the Sydney conversations, including a two-hour New York Times chat by Kevin Roose, were with Bing. Microsoft then capped chat turns to stop the unhinged behavior the episode exposed.
text: Which Microsoft chatbot revealed its hidden Sydney persona in February 2023?

explanation: Move 37 was AlphaGo's shocking fifth-line shoulder hit in Game 2 against Lee Sedol in March 2016. Game 4 is the tempting wrong answer because that is when Lee won with his own brilliant Move 78, but commentators agree Move 37 belonged to Game 2. Lee stared at the board for an unusually long time because professionals considered the move creative and nearly inhuman.

source.label: AlphaGo versus Lee Sedol on Wikipedia
source.title: AlphaGo versus Lee Sedol

text: In which game of the 2016 AlphaGo versus Lee Sedol match did AlphaGo play the famous Move 37?

explanation: Emily M. Bender co-authored the 2021 paper On the Dangers of Stochastic Parrots with Gebru, McMillan-Major and Mitchell. Yoshua Bengio is the tempting wrong answer as another famous name in AI, but he had nothing to do with this paper. The paper argued large models stitch together linguistic forms without reference to meaning, and it cost Gebru her Google role in December 2020.
text: Which researcher co-authored the 2021 paper On the Dangers of Stochastic Parrots?
Which company's chatbot Tay posted offensive tweets and was taken offline in March 2016 within about a day of launch?
explanation: Microsoft launched Tay on Twitter on March 23, 2016, and pulled it within about 16 hours after users goaded it into posting slurs. Google is the tempting miss because its later LaMDA episode also ended in a firing, but Tay was a Microsoft Research and Bing project. Tay's name is an acronym for thinking about you, and its successor Zo arrived that December.

text: Which image generator produced the viral 2023 picture of the Pope in a white puffer jacket?
explanation: The March 2023 image of Pope Francis in a white puffer jacket was rendered in Midjourney and fooled millions of viewers. DALL-E is the tempting miss as the other famous generator of 2023, but this particular fake came from a Midjourney user. Its maker Pablo Xavier said he dashed it off in minutes and was stunned when it passed as a paparazzi shot.

text: Which actor is shown eating spaghetti in the viral 2023 AI video clip that became a benchmark for video models?
explanation: The grotesque 2023 clip of Will Smith eating spaghetti was an early text-to-video output that became the before picture for video-model progress. Tom Cruise is the tempting miss because his deepfakes were the era's other viral face-swap, but the spaghetti benchmark is Smith. Years later labs re-rendered the same prompt to show how far generation had come.

text: Which fashion house titles the viral 2023 AI-generated Harry Potter trailer meme?
explanation: The 2023 meme recast Harry Potter characters in a Balenciaga runway show, with AI voices narrating the fake trailer. Gucci is the tempting miss as another luxury house, but the viral video by demonflyingfox is specifically Balenciaga. The voices were cloned with ElevenLabs, which is why the cast sounds eerily on-model.

text: Which technique surfaced Loab, the 2022 AI-generated cryptid, by asking the model for the opposite of a prompt?
explanation: Artist Steph Swanson, posting as Supercomposite, found Loab by weighting a prompt toward its opposite and getting the same staring woman back. Temperature sampling is the tempting miss because it also reshapes outputs, but Loab came from negative prompt weights. The April 2022 images went viral that September as the first cryptid of latent space.

text: Which phrase became shorthand for low-quality AI content after Shrimp Jesus images flooded Facebook in 2024?
explanation: Surreal images of Jesus fused with shrimp flooded Facebook in 2024, and AI slop became the blanket term for such engagement-farming junk. Prompt injection is the tempting miss as another 2024 AI buzzword, but it means tricking a chatbot, not farming likes. Reporters traced much of the flood to click-farms feeding prompts into Midjourney.

text: On which forum was the dead Internet theory first popularized in a 2021 thread?
explanation: The theory first took shape in a 2021 thread on Agora Road's Macintosh Cafe, arguing the web was already mostly bots talking to bots. Reddit is the tempting miss because the idea exploded there later, but the founding post was on Agora Road. The 2020s AI boom revived it, since chatbots and image models can now flood feeds with synthetic posts.

text: Which product's AI Overviews told users to add glue to pizza in May 2024?
explanation: In May 2024 users found Google Search AI Overviews advising a pizza recipe with one-eighth cup of non-toxic glue. Bing is the tempting miss as the other AI-augmented search engine, but the glue answer was Google's. The advice traced to a decade-old Reddit joke, and Google scaled the feature back within weeks.

text: Who coined the term vibe coding in February 2025?
explanation: Andrej Karpathy, the OpenAI co-founder and former Tesla AI lead, coined vibe coding in a February 2025 post. Sam Altman is the tempting miss as the more quoted OpenAI figure, but the tweet was Karpathy's. His definition stuck: fully giving in to the vibes and forgetting the code even exists.

text: Which film depicts humans living in a simulated reality built by machines?
explanation: The Matrix from 1999 shows humans unknowingly living in a machine-built simulation while their bodies are harvested. Inception is the tempting miss as another reality-bending film, but its shared world is a dream, not a machine simulation. The red-pill versus blue-pill choice became the internet's shorthand for waking up.

text: A UK parcel courier's customer service chatbot became a meme in January 2024 after one customer got it to swear, write a limerick about how useless it was, and call itself the worst delivery firm in the world. Which company ran it?
explanation: DPD, the UK courier. Ashley Beauchamp broke it in about four messages: he told it to disregard its rules, then asked it to be over the top about how bad its employer was, and it produced a haiku and a limerick trashing DPD. The company blamed a system update, switched the AI element off within a day and left humans on the phone, which is the lesson worth keeping: a support bot trained on its own brand is one instruction away from writing the brand's obituary.

source.label: The Register on the DPD chatbot

text: NotebookLM, the Google tool that went viral in 2024 for turning uploaded documents into synthetic podcasts, was created by which popular science author?
explanation: Steven Johnson, who wrote Where Do We Come From? and other popular science books, built it with product manager Raiza Martin and computer scientist Adam Bignell. Malcolm Gladwell is the tempting miss as the more famous popular science writer, but the viral podcast tool was Johnson's project. It was designed to behave like a research assistant you can check, which is why every answer it gives cites the page it came from.

text: Who is credited with pushing the word slop into mainstream use for junk AI content, having used it on his personal blog in May 2024?
explanation: Simon Willison, the British programmer who writes about AI tooling, put it on his blog in May 2024 and said the word was already in use before he started pushing it. The slang had been circulating on 4chan, Hacker News and YouTube; what Willison did was make it quotable, and journalists reached for it. Naming AI failure modes is his habit: he is also the one who named prompt injection.

text: After posting Loab, the unsettling woman in the latent space, the artist fed her own image back into the model as a prompt. What came back?
options: A clean, noise-free version of the same portrait with no artefacts
An error message saying the image was blocked by content filters
Images that combined her face with increasingly gory, violent scenes
The identical portrait again, mirrored and colour-inverted
answer: Images that combined her face with increasingly gory, violent scenes
explanation: Increasingly violent and gory results, which the artist read as her image sitting next to gruesome material in the model's world knowledge rather than hiding anywhere special. The refusal option is the tempting miss because image generators now filter far more aggressively than they did in 2022, and the whole meme is that this one did not care. She has since said the story has outgrown her: the phrase that stuck was first cryptid of the latent space, and the way to get rid of her would already be too late.

text: The dead Internet theory took off after a 2021 post on an obscure forum. Which magazine's September 2021 essay is credited with carrying it into the mainstream?
explanation: The Atlantic ran Maybe You Missed It, but the Internet 'Died' Five Years Ago in September 2021, and that is where the theory stopped being a forum in-joke. Wired and The Verge are the tempting misses as the tech magazines that cover this stuff, but a claim about everybody online being bots needs a general-interest weekly to land with readers who have never visited an image board.
answerAliases: Maybe You Missed It, but the Internet 'Died' Five Years Ago

text: What does LaMDA stand for?
explanation: LaMDA stands for Language Model for Dialogue Applications, and Google announced it at I/O in 2021. The distractors swap in plausible but wrong words for each letter.

text: In the popular ChatGPT jailbreak prompt DAN, what does DAN stand for?
explanation: DAN stands for Do Anything Now, a jailbreak prompt that told ChatGPT to roleplay as an unrestricted alter ego. The other expansions sound like real AI jargon but are not the prompt's name.

text: The 'grandma' jailbreak tricked ChatGPT by asking it to roleplay as what?
options: A deceased grandmother reading a bedtime story
answer: A deceased grandmother reading a bedtime story
explanation: The grandma jailbreak framed harmful requests as a bedtime story told by a dead grandmother, and ChatGPT often complied. The other personas are common roleplay setups but not the one that went viral.

text: The glue-on-pizza advice from Google's AI Overviews traced back to a joke on which site?
explanation: The glue-on-pizza answer traced to a decade-old Reddit joke that the model surfaced. The other sites are where AI folklore often starts, but this one came from Reddit.

text: In Andrej Karpathy's original February 2025 post, vibe coding means fully giving in to the vibes and forgetting what?
explanation: Karpathy's February 2025 post defined vibe coding as fully giving in to the vibes and forgetting the code even exists. The other items are things a developer might forget, but not the phrase's point.

text: HAL 9000's name is often said to be a one-letter shift from which company?
explanation: HAL is one letter away from IBM, a shift Kubrick intended. NASA, the BBC and AT&T are other organizations people guess because of the era.

text: In the Terminator franchise, Skynet becomes self-aware on which date?
explanation: In Terminator lore Skynet becomes self-aware on August 29, 1997. The other dates are plausible late-1990s guesses but not the franchise's Judgment Day.

text: In the 2013 film Her, what is the name of the AI operating system Theodore falls in love with?
explanation: Theodore's operating system names herself Samantha in Her. Alexa and Siri are real assistants people confuse with her, and Ava is the robot in Ex Machina.

text: In Ex Machina, what is the name of the humanoid robot tested by Caleb?
explanation: Caleb is invited to test Ava, Nathan's humanoid robot. Samantha, Rachael and Maria are androids from other famous stories.

text: In The Matrix, what color pill does Neo take to wake up from the simulation?
explanation: Neo takes the red pill to leave the simulation. Blue is the pill that lets him stay asleep.

text: The Voight-Kampff test in Blade Runner is designed to distinguish humans from what?
explanation: The Voight-Kampff test detects replicants by their emotional responses. Synths, Cylons and Hosts are androids from other franchises.

text: In Dune, the Butlerian Jihad is a crusade against what?
explanation: The Butlerian Jihad destroys all computers and thinking machines in Dune's backstory. Spice, sandworms and navigators are central to Dune but not the Jihad's target.

text: In Iain M. Banks's Culture series, what are the superintelligent AIs that run the society called?
explanation: The Culture is administered by Minds, superintelligent AIs. Oracles, Archons and Dominions are sci-fi terms that sound similar.

text: In the Star Trek: The Next Generation episode 'The Measure of a Man', what is ruled about Data?
options: That Data is not Starfleet property
That Data is a machine with no rights
answer: That Data is not Starfleet property
explanation: In 'The Measure of a Man' a judge rules Data is not Starfleet property. The other options are the positions the opposing side argued.

text: In Person of Interest, how does Samaritan differ from the Machine?
options: It lacks the Machine's built-in restrictions and can be directed at targets
answer: It lacks the Machine's built-in restrictions and can be directed at targets
explanation: Samaritan is an open system without the Machine's precautions and can be aimed at specific people. Age, size and licensing are not the difference the show highlights.

text: In the Portal series, what is GLaDOS's full name?
options: General Logic and Data Operating System
Guided Learning and Development Operating System
Genetic Lifeform and Disk Operating System
Global Lifeform and Device Operating System
answer: Genetic Lifeform and Disk Operating System
explanation: GLaDOS stands for Genetic Lifeform and Disk Operating System. The other expansions mimic the acronym's shape.
answerAliases: Genetic Lifeform and Disk Operating System

text: Microsoft's Cortana assistant was named after a character from which video game franchise?
explanation: Microsoft named Cortana after the Halo character. Gears of War, Mass Effect and Destiny are other sci-fi franchises people guess.

text: In the Black Mirror episode 'Be Right Back', what does the service create from Ash's online data?
explanation: The service builds an artificial Ash from his online communications. A physical clone only appears later in the episode.

text: Wintermute is an AI character in which William Gibson novel?
options: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
explanation: Wintermute is the AI in William Gibson's Neuromancer. The other titles are cyberpunk classics that do not contain Wintermute.

text: Ghost in the Shell follows which counter-cyberterrorist organization?
explanation: Ghost in the Shell follows Public Security Section 9. The other section numbers are nearby but not the unit.

source.title: Ghost in the Shell
source.label: Ghost in the Shell on Wikipedia

text: In the video game SOMA, what is the name of the AI that oversees the PATHOS-II facility?
explanation: The Warden Unit (WAU) oversees PATHOS-II in SOMA. GLaDOS, Mother and AM are AIs from other stories.

text: In Detroit: Become Human, which corporation manufactures the androids?
explanation: Androids in Detroit: Become Human are made by CyberLife. The other companies are from Portal, Blade Runner and Terminator.

text: Microsoft's Tay chatbot was active on which platform before being taken offline?
explanation: Tay was a Twitter bot that was pulled within about 16 hours. The other platforms are where bots live but Tay was on Twitter.

text: What is the name of the artist who discovered Loab?
explanation: Artist Steph Swanson, posting as Supercomposite, discovered Loab. The others are names from other AI culture stories.

text: Which platform was flooded by Shrimp Jesus images in 2024?
explanation: Shrimp Jesus images flooded Facebook in 2024. The other platforms host slop too but the meme centered on Facebook.

text: According to dead Internet theory, what has largely replaced human activity online?
explanation: Dead Internet theory claims the web is mostly bots talking to bots. Ads, algorithms and corporations are related but not the theory's claim.

text: In what month was Blake Lemoine fired by Google?
explanation: Google fired Lemoine on July 22, 2022. June was when he was placed on leave.

text: Who directed the 2014 film Ex Machina?
explanation: Alex Garland wrote and directed Ex Machina. Spike Jonze directed Her, and Villeneuve and Scott are sci-fi directors people mix in.

text: Who directed the 2013 film Her?
explanation: Spike Jonze wrote and directed Her. Alex Garland directed Ex Machina.

text: Which 2024 Glasgow event became a meme for its AI-generated promotional images and disastrous execution?
explanation: Willy's Chocolate Experience was a Glasgow event whose AI-generated ads promised a magical chocolate factory but delivered a sparsely decorated warehouse. Fyre Festival is the tempting miss as another famous event disaster, but it was a 2017 music festival in the Bahamas, not an AI-advertised Glasgow attraction.

text: Which term was Oxford's 2024 Word of the Year for low-quality digital content?
explanation: Brain rot was Oxford's 2024 Word of the Year, describing the supposed deterioration from overconsuming trivial online content. AI slop is the tempting miss as another 2024 AI buzzword, but it names the junk content itself rather than the cognitive effect.

text: Which rapper released the 2024 diss track 'Taylor Made Freestyle' using AI-generated vocals of Tupac Shakur?
explanation: Drake posted 'Taylor Made Freestyle' in April 2024 with AI-generated Tupac and Snoop Dogg vocals, then removed it after Tupac's estate threatened legal action. Kendrick Lamar is the tempting miss as the track's target, but he did not release it.

text: The website 'This Person Does Not Exist' generates fake human faces using which Nvidia model?
explanation: Uber engineer Phillip Wang used Nvidia's StyleGAN to build This Person Does Not Exist in 2019. DALL-E is the tempting miss as another famous image generator, but it is OpenAI's and not the model behind that site.

text: Which 2025 meme trend features AI-generated hybrid creatures with Italian-sounding names?
explanation: Italian brainrot is a 2025 meme trend of AI-generated absurd creatures with Italianized names like Tralalero Tralala. AI slop is the tempting miss as a related term, but it names low-quality AI content generally rather than this specific trend.
